iom_applies_to: Preformed vitamin A only (retinol and retinyl esters). Does not cover beta-carotene or other carotenoids.
efsa_applies_to: Preformed vitamin A only (retinol and retinyl esters), total intake from all sources. Applies to all adults including women of child-bearing age, pregnant, lactating and post-menopausal women.
lowest_applies_to: Preformed vitamin A (retinol + retinyl esters), total intake from food, fortified foods and supplements
notes: IOM and EFSA agree at 3000 µg/day. Both count preformed vitamin A only, not beta-carotene. 1 µg RE = 1 µg retinol; EFSA gives 1 mg RE = 3333.33 IU, so 3000 µg = 10,000 IU of retinol. EFSA 2024 set no UL for beta-carotene: smokers should avoid beta-carotene supplements. Older UK EVM guidance (1500 µg/day) is not used because both IOM and EFSA have a UL.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food, water and supplements (vitamin D2 + D3). 100 µg = 4,000 IU.
efsa_applies_to: Total intake from all sources, including fortified foods and food supplements. Covers vitamin D2, vitamin D3 and calcidiol monohydrate (1 µg VDE = 1 µg D3 = 1 µg D2 = 0.4 µg calcidiol monohydrate = 40 IU).
lowest_applies_to: Total vitamin D (D2 + D3) from all sources
notes: IOM and EFSA agree at 100 µg/day (4,000 IU). Unit: 1 µg = 40 IU. EFSA 2023 counts calcidiol monohydrate at 2.5x (0.4 µg calcidiol monohydrate = 1 µg VDE, valid up to 10 µg/day calcidiol).

iom_applies_to: Supplemental alpha-tocopherol only (any form of supplemental alpha-tocopherol, all 8 stereoisomers). Applies to synthetic forms from supplements, fortified foods or both; not food vitamin E.
efsa_applies_to: Alpha-tocopherol from all dietary sources, all stereoisomeric forms (natural RRR and synthetic all-rac). Does not apply to people on anticoagulant or antiplatelet drugs (e.g. aspirin), on secondary CVD prevention, or with vitamin K malabsorption.
lowest_applies_to: Alpha-tocopherol, all forms, total intake from all sources (EFSA)
notes: Big difference: IOM 1000 mg vs EFSA 300 mg. EFSA (2024 review) kept 300 mg/day. Converting IU: per ODS, 1 IU natural (RRR) = 0.67 mg and 1 IU synthetic (all-rac) = 0.45 mg alpha-tocopherol. So 300 mg = about 448 IU natural or about 667 IU synthetic. Note: EFSA's 2024 opinion uses a different all-rac factor (1 IU all-rac acetate = 1 mg acetate = 0.91 mg free alpha-tocopherol), so convert IU carefully. Warn users on blood thinners regardless of dose.

iom_applies_to: No UL set (not determinable).
efsa_applies_to: No UL (SCF 2003: no appropriate data to set one). No adverse effects seen with supplemental phylloquinone up to 10 mg/day for limited periods. People on coumarin anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin) should not raise vitamin K intake without medical advice.
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental vitamin K (UK EVM guidance level, used because IOM and EFSA have no UL)
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = 1 mg/day (1000 µg) supplemental. EVM value taken from secondary sources (Danish 2006 table: 1000 µg GL; NHS: 'Taking 1mg or less of vitamin K supplements a day is unlikely to cause any harm'). The EVM 2003 PDF itself could not be downloaded to confirm. Key safety issue is a drug interaction, not toxicity: flag any vitamin K for warfarin users.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food and supplements.
efsa_applies_to: No UL (EFSA 2004: insufficient data). EFSA stated supplemental doses up to about 1 g/day on top of normal diet are not associated with adverse gastrointestinal effects. This is a statement, not a formal UL or safe level.
lowest_applies_to: Total vitamin C from food and supplements (IOM)
notes: Only IOM has a UL (2000 mg/day). EFSA has none, but noted no GI effects from supplements up to about 1 g/day (1000 mg) and GI effects at 3-4 g/day. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = 1000 mg/day supplemental (via EFSA 2004 opinion and NHS: 'less than 1,000mg of vitamin C supplements a day'). EVM value not used for 'lowest' because an IOM UL exists. A more cautious app could warn at 1000 mg supplemental.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food and supplements. Not for people taking high doses under medical supervision.
efsa_applies_to: No EFSA UL found. Choline is not listed in EFSA's UL overview (Version 11, Aug 2025).
lowest_applies_to: Total choline from food and supplements (IOM)
notes: Only IOM has a UL: 3.5 g/day = 3,500 mg/day. EFSA has not set a UL for choline (not in its UL overview); efsa_year left null.

iom_applies_to: No UL set (lack of suitable data).
efsa_applies_to: No UL (SCF 2001: no adequate data to derive a UL).
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental thiamin (UK EVM guidance level; water-soluble forms)
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = 100 mg/day supplemental thiamin (applies to water-soluble forms of thiamin). Taken from secondary sources (Danish 2006 table; NHS: 'Taking 100mg or less a day of thiamin supplements is unlikely to cause any harm'). EVM PDF itself not downloadable to confirm.

iom_applies_to: No UL set (lack of suitable data).
efsa_applies_to: No UL (SCF 2000: no adequate data to derive a UL).
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental riboflavin (UK EVM guidance level)
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = 40 mg/day supplemental riboflavin (Danish 2006 table; NHS: 'Taking 40mg or less a day of riboflavin supplements is unlikely to cause any harm'). EVM PDF not downloadable to confirm.

iom_applies_to: Supplemental and fortified-food niacin only (synthetic forms). Covers BOTH nicotinic acid and nicotinamide (niacinamide). Does not count niacin naturally in food. Not for use under medical supervision.
efsa_applies_to: Two separate ULs: free nicotinic acid 10 mg/day; nicotinamide 900 mg/day. Adult values do not apply in pregnancy or lactation (inadequate data). Not for clinical use (e.g. treating high cholesterol).
lowest_applies_to: Free nicotinic acid (EFSA). For nicotinamide use IOM 35 mg/day (supplemental), since EFSA's nicotinamide UL is 900 mg/day.
notes: Form matters. EFSA: nicotinic acid 10 mg/day, nicotinamide 900 mg/day (about 12.5 mg/kg bw). IOM: 35 mg/day for all supplemental niacin, both forms. Lowest by form: nicotinic acid = 10 mg (EFSA); nicotinamide = 35 mg (IOM). If the app cannot tell the form, use 10 mg/day. UK EVM guidance (17 mg nicotinic acid, 500 mg nicotinamide) not used because IOM and EFSA have ULs. Inositol hexanicotinate etc. not separately assessed in these sources.

iom_applies_to: No UL set (lack of suitable data).
efsa_applies_to: No UL (SCF 2002: no adequate data to derive a UL).
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental pantothenic acid (UK EVM guidance level)
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = 200 mg/day supplemental pantothenic acid (Danish 2006 table; NHS: 'Taking 200mg or less a day of pantothenic acid in supplements is unlikely to cause any harm'). EVM PDF not downloadable to confirm.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food and supplements.
efsa_applies_to: Total intake from all dietary sources and all vitamin B6 vitamers (pyridoxine, pyridoxal, pyridoxamine and their forms). Includes pregnant and lactating women.
lowest_applies_to: Total vitamin B6 from all sources, all vitamers (EFSA)
notes: Big difference: IOM 100 mg vs EFSA 12 mg. EFSA cut its UL from 25 mg (SCF 2000) to 12 mg in 2023 because of peripheral neuropathy. EFSA's news text says 12.5 mg/day, but the opinion abstract and the UL overview both give the final adult UL as 12 mg/day (midpoint of 12.5 and 11.7, rounded down). Use 12. UK EVM 10 mg/day supplemental SUL exists but is not used because IOM and EFSA have ULs.

iom_applies_to: No UL set (lack of suitable data).
efsa_applies_to: No UL (SCF 2001: no adequate data to derive a UL).
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental biotin (UK EVM guidance level)
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = 0.9 mg/day (900 µg) supplemental biotin; total intake about 0.97 mg/day. Supplemental value read from the EVM 2003 PDF (via WebFetch) and matched by the Danish 2006 table (900 µg) and NHS ('0.9mg or less a day of biotin in supplements').

iom_applies_to: Folic acid from supplements and fortified foods only (synthetic folate). Not food folate. Value is in µg folic acid, NOT µg DFE.
efsa_applies_to: Combined intake of folic acid, (6S)-5-methyltetrahydrofolic acid glucosamine and L-5-methyltetrahydrofolic acid calcium salt added to foods or in supplements. Does not include natural food folate.
lowest_applies_to: Synthetic folate (folic acid + authorised methylfolate salts) from supplements and fortified foods; not food folate
notes: IOM and EFSA agree at 1000 µg/day. Unit trap: the UL is µg of folic acid, not µg DFE. 1 µg DFE = 0.6 µg folic acid with food, so a label saying 1667 µg DFE = 1000 µg folic acid. EFSA (2023) counts methylfolate (5-MTHF) salts in the same UL; the IOM UL refers to synthetic folate generally. EFSA 2023 kept the SCF value.

iom_applies_to: No UL set (lack of suitable data).
efsa_applies_to: No UL (SCF 2000: no defined adverse effects; not possible to derive a UL).
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental vitamin B12 (UK EVM guidance level)
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = 2000 µg/day (2 mg) supplemental B12 (Danish 2006 table; NHS: 'Taking 2mg or less a day of vitamin B12 in supplements is unlikely to cause any harm'). EVM PDF not downloadable to confirm.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food and supplements. 2500 mg/day for ages 19-50; 2000 mg/day for ages 51+. Value shown is the 51+ figure (most conservative adult value).
efsa_applies_to: Total intake from diet and supplements, adults including pregnant and lactating women.
lowest_applies_to: Total calcium from food and supplements (IOM, ages 51+); 2500 mg/day if the user is 19-50
notes: IOM UL depends on age: 2500 mg (19-50) and 2000 mg (51+). EFSA: 2500 mg for all adults. So IOM and EFSA agree for 19-50 and differ for 51+. Recommend the app uses 2000 mg if age is 51+ or unknown, else 2500 mg. UK EVM guidance (1500 mg supplemental) not used because IOM and EFSA have ULs.

iom_applies_to: Supplemental magnesium only (pharmacological agents: supplements and medications). Does not include magnesium in food and water.
efsa_applies_to: Readily dissociable magnesium salts (e.g. chloride, sulphate, aspartate, lactate) and compounds like MgO in food supplements, water or added to foods. Does not include magnesium naturally in food and drinks.
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental / added magnesium only (EFSA); not food magnesium
notes: IOM 350 mg vs EFSA 250 mg; both count supplemental (added) magnesium only. Do NOT add food magnesium to the total. Note the scope difference: EFSA also counts magnesium in water and added to foods. EFSA's UL is from SCF 2001 and has not been re-evaluated. UK EVM guidance (400 mg supplemental) not used because IOM and EFSA have ULs.

iom_applies_to: No UL set (2019 NASEM review: not determinable owing to lack of data on a specific toxicological adverse effect).
efsa_applies_to: No UL (EFSA 2005: data insufficient). EFSA noted long-term intakes of about 3 g/day of potassium as potassium chloride supplements, on top of food, did not cause adverse effects in healthy adults; GI symptoms seen with some supplement forms at 1-5 g/day. Not a formal UL or safe level.
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental potassium (UK EVM guidance level); not for people with impaired kidney function, older people, or those on drugs affecting potassium balance
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = 3700 mg/day supplemental potassium (Danish 2006 table; NHS: 'Taking 3,700mg or less of potassium supplements a day is unlikely to have obvious harmful effects'). EVM PDF not downloadable to confirm. EFSA's 3 g/day statement is a no-adverse-effect observation, not a limit. EFSA and NHS both flag higher-risk groups: impaired kidney function, older people, people on cardiovascular drugs or drugs affecting potassium balance, diabetes. NHS: older people should not take potassium supplements unless advised by a doctor. The app should warn these groups at any supplemental dose.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food and supplements (UL based on GI effects of supplemental iron).
efsa_applies_to: Total iron intake from diet and supplements, adults including pregnant and lactating women. Safe level of intake, not a UL (EFSA could not set a UL). EFSA notes people with haemochromatosis are particularly sensitive to iron overload and are not the target population (they are managed through medical care).
lowest_applies_to: Total iron from food and supplements (EFSA safe level of intake)
notes: IOM 45 mg (UL) vs EFSA 40 mg (safe level of intake, 2024). EFSA says a safe level is weaker than a UL: going above it does not prove harm, but it is the highest level with reasonable confidence of no adverse effects. Using it as the ceiling is the cautious choice. People with haemochromatosis should not take iron supplements without medical advice. UK EVM 17 mg supplemental guidance level not used because IOM and EFSA have values.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food, water and supplements.
efsa_applies_to: Total intake from all sources; adults including pregnant and lactating women.
lowest_applies_to: Total zinc from food and supplements (EFSA)
notes: IOM 40 mg vs EFSA 25 mg. EFSA's UL is from SCF 2002 (not re-evaluated); SCF based it on effects of high zinc on copper status. UK EVM 25 mg supplemental SUL exists but is not used because IOM and EFSA have ULs.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food, water and supplements. 10,000 µg/day converted to 10 mg/day.
efsa_applies_to: Total intake from all sources. Adult UL does not apply in pregnancy or lactation (inadequate data).
lowest_applies_to: Total copper from food, water and supplements (EFSA)
notes: IOM 10 mg (table lists 10,000 µg/day; converted to mg) vs EFSA 5 mg. EFSA UL is from SCF 2003. In 2023 the EFSA Scientific Committee also set an ADI of 0.07 mg/kg bw (about 4.9 mg/day at 70 kg) and said no copper retention is expected at 5 mg/day, so 5 mg/day remains a sound ceiling. UK EVM 10 mg total SUL not used because IOM and EFSA have ULs.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food and supplements.
efsa_applies_to: Total intake from all dietary sources, adults including pregnant and lactating women.
lowest_applies_to: Total selenium from food and supplements (EFSA)
notes: IOM 400 µg vs EFSA 255 µg. EFSA lowered its UL from 300 µg (SCF 2000) to 255 µg in 2023, based on alopecia (hair loss). EFSA says adults are unlikely to exceed it except regular users of high-dose selenium supplements or regular consumers of Brazil nuts. UK EVM 450 µg total SUL not used because IOM and EFSA have ULs.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food and supplements.
efsa_applies_to: Total intake from all sources; adults including pregnant and lactating women. Not for populations with iodine deficiency disorders or people treated with iodine under medical supervision.
lowest_applies_to: Total iodine from food and supplements (EFSA)
notes: IOM 1100 µg vs EFSA 600 µg. EFSA UL is from SCF 2002 (not re-evaluated). UK EVM 500 µg supplemental guidance level not used because IOM and EFSA have ULs.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food, water and supplements.
efsa_applies_to: Total manganese intake from all dietary sources, including fortified foods and food supplements. Adults 18+ including pregnant and lactating women. Safe level of intake, not a UL.
lowest_applies_to: Total manganese from food and supplements (EFSA safe level of intake)
notes: IOM 11 mg (UL) vs EFSA 8 mg (safe level of intake, 2023). EFSA's 8 mg is based on high background diet intakes (P95), not on a toxicity threshold, because data were insufficient for a UL. Main food sources per EFSA: grains, tea and fruit (a 200 mL cup of tea may contain 300-1000 µg). UK EVM 4 mg supplemental guidance level (0.5 mg for older people) not used because IOM and EFSA have values.

iom_applies_to: No UL set (lack of suitable data).
efsa_applies_to: No UL (SCF 2003: data insufficient for trivalent chromium Cr(III)).
lowest_applies_to: Total trivalent chromium Cr(III) (UK EVM guidance level); excludes chromium picolinate
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 guidance level = about 0.15 mg/kg bw/day trivalent chromium, i.e. about 10 mg/day (10,000 µg) for a 60 kg adult, total intake. It applies only to trivalent chromium and explicitly EXCLUDES chromium picolinate (possible DNA damage in vitro). Value confirmed via EFSA/SCF 2003 chromium opinion and Irish FSAI report quoting the EVM; NHS: '10mg or less a day of chromium from food and supplements'. EVM PDF not downloadable. Note WHO (1996) advised supplements should not exceed 250 µg/day, far lower than the EVM level - a cautious app may prefer 250 µg for supplements, especially picolinate.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food, water and supplements.
efsa_applies_to: Total intake from all sources; adults including pregnant and lactating women. Summary table lists 0.6 mg/day.
lowest_applies_to: Total molybdenum from food and supplements (EFSA)
notes: IOM 2000 µg vs EFSA 600 µg. EFSA's UL (0.6 mg/day = 600 µg/day, about 0.01 mg/kg bw) is from SCF 2000 and has not been re-evaluated; converted from mg to µg. UK EVM: the 2003 executive summary lists molybdenum among nutrients given 'guidance', but no number could be verified (that EVM section was not readable, and the Danish 2006 summary table shows no EVM value). Not needed here because IOM and EFSA both have ULs.

iom_applies_to: Total intake from food, water and supplements.
efsa_applies_to: Boron as boric acid and borates only; adults including pregnant and lactating women (0.16 mg/kg bw/day).
lowest_applies_to: Total boron (as boric acid/borates) from food, water and supplements (EFSA)
notes: IOM 20 mg vs EFSA 10 mg. For reference, UK EVM 2003 SUL = 0.16 mg/kg bw/day, i.e. 9.6 mg/day for a 60 kg adult (total intake). EVM value confirmed via EFSA 2004 boron opinion ('EGVM upper safe level is 0.16 mg boron/kg body weight/day') and Danish 2006 table (9.6 mg, 60 kg adult). 'lowest' uses EFSA (10 mg) per the rule; EVM's 9.6 mg is effectively the same per-kg limit at a lower reference body weight. A cautious app could use 9.6 mg.

iom_applies_to: No UL set. NASEM notes there is no justification for adding silicon to supplements.
efsa_applies_to: No UL (EFSA 2004: data inadequate). Usual diet intakes (20-50 mg/day) considered not harmful.
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental silicon (UK EVM SUL; 60 kg adult). Total-intake SUL about 760 mg/day.
notes: No IOM or EFSA UL. UK EVM 2003 SUL = 25 mg silicon dioxide/kg bw/day for supplemental intake, i.e. about 700 mg silicon/day for a 60 kg adult; total intake SUL estimated at 760 mg/day. Value confirmed via BfR 2021 silicon opinion quoting the EVM, and EFSA 2009 (ANS Panel) used 700 mg/day as the reference. EVM PDF not downloadable to confirm directly. Caution: EFSA only assessed some forms at lower amounts (e.g. silica gel up to 200 mg Si/day; choline-stabilised orthosilicic acid and MMST up to 10 mg Si/day). Danish 2006 table lists 1500 mg for silicon (that is the silicon dioxide amount, = 700 mg Si) - do not use 1500 as silicon.

iom_applies_to: No UL set for any omega-3 (ALA, EPA, DHA). IOM noted high EPA+DHA (900 mg EPA + 600 mg DHA or more for several weeks) might reduce immune function.
efsa_applies_to: EPA + DHA combined, supplemental intake, adults. EFSA set no UL (2012) but said long-term supplemental EPA+DHA combined up to about 5 g/day does not raise safety concerns; EPA alone up to 1.8 g/day also fine. Separate safe level for DHA alone: 1 g/day (re-confirmed 2026) for products that are DHA-only or mostly DHA (EPA/DHA ratio < 0.3).
lowest_applies_to: Supplemental EPA + DHA combined (EFSA safe intake statement). DHA-only products: 1 g/day DHA.
notes: Neither IOM nor EFSA set a UL. EFSA 2012: combined EPA+DHA up to about 5 g/day (5000 mg) supplemental is safe for adults - a 'no safety concern' statement, recorded here as safe level of intake. EFSA 2026 formally kept a safe level of intake of 1 g/day for supplemental DHA alone (all groups) when the source has EPA/DHA ratio < 0.3 (e.g. algal DHA oils). The FDA (via ODS) also says supplements giving no more than 5 g/day EPA+DHA are safe. Recommend the app warns at 5 g EPA+DHA, and at 1 g DHA if the product is DHA-only.
